title: Florida Atlantic University Launches Executive Certificate in Quantum Computing Strategy - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Florida Atlantic University's College of Business launched an eight-week, $2,700 executive certificate, "Quantum Computing: Business and Sourcing Strategy," aimed at non-technical enterprise leaders and procurement directors rather than physicists. The course follows FAU's $20 million agreement with D-Wave to install a 4,400+ qubit Advantage2 annealing system on the Boca Raton campus, the first dedicated on-premises university quantum computer in Florida.

themes.theme: Quantum procurement becomes an executive discipline

insights.claim: Florida Atlantic University's College of Business Executive Education program launched an eight-week certificate, "Quantum Computing: Business and Sourcing Strategy," targeting non-technical enterprise leaders, technology executives, procurement directors and strategists.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Business schools building sourcing curricula signals that quantum buying decisions are moving from research labs to procurement budgets.
insights.locator: Opening paragraph — "The Executive Education program in the College of Business"

insights.claim: The FAU course runs August 24 to October 12, 2026, covers 24 hours of instruction at $2,700 tuition, and is offered both on the Boca Raton campus and via live virtual sessions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A low-priced, short-format executive product is designed for volume — a cheap read on how broad corporate quantum interest actually is.
insights.locator: "Scheduled to run from August 24 to October 12, 2026"

insights.claim: The curriculum explicitly teaches evaluation across the vendor ecosystem — IBM Quantum, Google Quantum AI, D-Wave, IonQ, Quantinuum, AWS Braket and Azure Quantum — plus Quantum-as-a-Service procurement and post-quantum cryptography risk management.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Comparative vendor evaluation frameworks entering executive education mean quantum vendors will increasingly compete on procurement criteria, not just qubit counts.

insights.claim: The FAU program is led by Dr. Mehran Basiratmand, Director of Innovation and Programs, alongside College of Business Dean Dr. Daniel Gropper.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Dean-level sponsorship indicates institutional commitment rather than a one-off elective.
insights.locator: "Led by Dr. Mehran Basiratmand, Director of Innovation and Programs"

themes.theme: On-premises D-Wave system as regional anchor

insights.claim: FAU signed a $20 million agreement with D-Wave Quantum Inc. to install an on-site 4,400+ qubit Advantage2 annealing quantum computer at its Boca Raton campus.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A $20M university system sale is material for an annealing vendor with low single-digit-million quarterly revenue — the kind of deal that moves bookings.
insights.quote: FAU’s landmark $20 million agreement with D-Wave Quantum Inc. to install an on-site, 4,400+ qubit Advantage2™ annealing quantum computer at its Boca Raton campus

insights.claim: The installation makes FAU the first university in Florida to host a dedicated on-premises quantum system, positioning South Florida as an emerging regional hub for hybrid quantum research, defense application development and workforce training.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: On-prem university systems seed regional talent and defense pipelines — a leading indicator of where quantum clusters form next.
insights.locator: "The installation makes FAU the first university in Florida"

insights.claim: FAU is pairing hardware ownership with executive education, using the certificate program as a commercial-facing follow-on to its quantum computer installation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-plus-training bundles let vendors monetize an installed base through the surrounding ecosystem rather than the box alone.
insights.locator: "The educational initiative follows FAU’s landmark $20 million agreement"
